name: Copy and UX Writing Rulebook
summary: Words that sound like the business and help people act: headlines, buttons, errors, claims.
check: Read every button out of context; it says what happens.
Search the copy for buzzwords, em dashes and "Oops".

rules.title: Write like the business talks
rules.text: Use the client's own words from their brief, their menus, their emails. A bakery does not "empower"; it bakes.

rules.title: Specific beats clever
rules.text: Name the thing, the number, the place and the time: "Fresh bread from 7:00, Vinohradská 12" beats "Crafted with passion".

rules.title: Buzzwords
rules.text: Avoid "seamless", "unlock", "elevate", "empower", "revolutionise", "next-level", "cutting-edge", "game-changing", "supercharge", "effortless", "delve", "leverage", "robust", "in today's fast-paced world", and the newer AI tells "quiet" (quiet confidence, quietly powerful), "real" (real results, real people), "crafted" and "thoughtfully".

rules.title: Slogan rhythm
rules.text: Avoid three-word fragments in a row, rhetorical questions as headings, and "not X but Y" contrasts (`SL-38`, `SL-71`).

rules.title: Short sentences, plain words
rules.text: Most sentences under about 20 words; one idea per sentence.

rules.title: Front-load
rules.text: The important word comes first in headings, buttons and list items, so scanning works.

rules.title: Buttons say what happens
rules.text: Verb plus object: "Book a table", "Download the menu", "Save changes". The button keeps the same words as the heading or link that led to it (`SL-41`).

rules.title: Consistent terms
rules.text: One name per thing across the whole site ("basket" or "cart", never both).

rules.title: Sentence case
rules.text: Headings, buttons and labels in sentence case unless the brand insists otherwise.

rules.title: Error messages: what, why, how to fix
rules.text: "This card has expired. Use another card or update the expiry date." Never blame the user, never "Invalid input", never only a code.

rules.title: Empty states invite
rules.text: Say what will be here and how to start (`ST-01`).

rules.title: Confirmations name the result
rules.text: "Order 4821 is placed. We will email you when it ships." (`ST-10`).

rules.title: Permission and data requests explain why
rules.text: Say what you need and what the user gets for it, at the moment you ask (`PL-04`).

rules.title: Invented claims, numbers or customers
rules.text: No invented numbers, customers, awards or reviews. Placeholders are marked as placeholders for the client to replace (`SL-42` to `SL-44`).

rules.title: Numerals for numbers
rules.text: Write numbers as digits ("3 days", "12 %") in interfaces; they scan faster than words.

rules.title: Write for scanning
rules.text: Short paragraphs, meaningful subheadings, lists for steps and options, the key point first.

rules.title: Unambiguous dates and times
rules.text: Write dates in a format nobody misreads ("17 Nov 2026", "Tue 9:00–17:00") and show time zones where they matter.

rules.title: Inclusive, plain language
rules.text: Gender-neutral wording, no idioms that do not translate, explain necessary jargon once.

rules.title: Cute error messages
rules.text: No "Oops!", "Uh-oh" or jokes in errors. People with a problem want the cause and the fix.

rules.title: Exclamation marks everywhere
rules.text: At most one exclamation mark on a page, saved for real good news.

rules.title: All-caps for emphasis
rules.text: Do not shout. Use weight or placement for emphasis, never capitals in sentences.

rules.title: Placeholder copy in a design
rules.text: No lorem ipsum in reviewed designs. Write real or realistic copy; placeholder text hides layout problems.
